'''Milko Borissov Ivanov''' (18 February 1921 – 5 October 1998) was a Bulgarian physicist,<ref>Л. Спасов, Г. Камишева, 100 години от рождението на академик Милко Борисов, Списание на БАН (2) 47-50 (2021)</ref> member of the [[Bulgarian Academy of Sciences]] (BAS), university professor, founder of the Institute of Solid State Physics of the BAS and its director  (1973–1991).<ref>Л. Спасов, Г. Камишева, "Милко Борисов за себе си и другите за него", София, Акад. изд. "Проф. М. Дринов" (2008)</ref><ref>{{cite book |title=Who's who in Science in Europe: A Biographical Guide in Science, Technology, Agriculture, and Medicine |volume=4 |publisher=Longman |year= 1991 |edition= 7th |page=[https://archive.org/details/whoswhoinscience0004unse_7ed/page/47/mode/2up?view=theater 47] |isbn=9780582086623 |url=https://archive.org/details/whoswhoinscience0004unse_7ed/page/n3/mode/2up |url-access=registration |via= [[Internet Archive]]}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Milko Borissov was born in [[Sofia]] 18 February 1921. He studied physics at [[Sofia University]] from 1939 to 1943. After [[World War II]], he was assistant (1945–1948), associate professor and full professor.<ref>И. Лалов, "Слово за моя учител. По случай 75-годишнината на акад. М. Борисов". Светът на физиката (1996), кн.2, с.117-123</ref> He lectured on courses in General Physics, Introduction to Solid State Physics and the Physical foundation of acoustic electronics and acoustic optics  and published university textbooks on them. He could use both [[Germany]] and [[Russia]].{{clarify|date=October 2026}}<ref>А. Апостолов, Ю. Буров, "Чл.-кор. проф. Милко Борисов на 60 години", Физика (1981), кн. 1, с.23-24</ref> He was dean of the Physics and Mathematics Faculty and Sofia University deputy rector.{{Citation needed|date=February 2026}}

He was deputy director of the BAS [[Institute of Physics]] and director of the Institute of Solid-State Physics and United Centre of Physics (1973–1988).<ref>Е. Леяровски, "Академик Милко Борисов на 70 години". Светът на физиката (1991), кн.1, с.45</ref> He became a member of BAS.<ref>Л. Спасов, Г. Камишева, 100 години от рождението на академик Милко Борисов - бележит учител на поколения български физици и строител на българската физика през втората половина на ХХ век, Списание на БАН, кн. 2, с. 47-50 (2021)</ref>

Borissov died in Sofia on 5 November 1998.<ref>G. Kamisheva Traditions and Reforms in Bulgarian Physics. Milko Borissov (1921–1998). – CP1203 7th International Conference of the Balkan Physical Union, Edited by A. Angelopoulos and T. Fildisis, AIP (2009) 1336–1341</ref>

== Contributions ==
Borissov worked in the area of [[solid state physics]].<ref>А. Ваврек, Академик Милко Борисов и развитието на физиката на твърдото тяло в България", Списание на БАН (1999), кн. 3-4, с. 70-77</ref> He initiated investigations in the area of acoustoelectronics in Bulgaria for the first time. He studied [[Plasma (physics)|plasma physics]] and paramagnetic resonance. He organised and headed a history of physics group at the Institute of Solid-State physics, and published two books about physics in Bulgarian schools. He had 15 patents and supervised 10 PhD students.<ref>М. Замфиров, "85 години от раждането на акад. Милко Борисов", сп. Физика (2006) кн. 3, с. 178-182</ref>

== Recognition ==
A street is named Milko Borissov in Sofia's district [[Vitosha]] ({{maplink|type=line|id=Q123951657|title=Проф. Милко Борисов}}).

A session dedicated to Borissov's memory was organised in 2003. Proceedings were published in 2006.<ref>А. Г. Петров, И. Илиев (ред), "Сесия в памет на академик Милко Борисов (17.10.2003 г.)", Сборник научни доклади, Унив.изд. "Епископ Константин Преславски", Шумен (2006)</ref> The next memorial session marked the 90-year anniversary of Borissov's birth, on 18 February 2011.
